sections.title: Letter ipszilon
paragraphs: You name this letter (ipszilon) /ipsilon/. Its main sound is a consonant, as in (yacht) /ˈjɒht/, which means a sailing boat. Consonant means a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter has two sounds.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue toward the roof. Keep the air flowing smoothly through the small gap. For the second sound, raise your tongue high and forward in your mouth. Keep your lips spread wide. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the vibration of your voice.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: In foreign loanwords, you say the consonant sound, as in (yoga) /ˈjoːɡɒ/. In old family names with traditional spelling, you say the vowel sound, as in (Báthory) /ˈbaːtori/ or (Kölcsey) /ˈkølt͡ʃɛi/. Vowel means a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the vowel sound into a diphthong like the end of fly. A diphthong means two vowel sounds in one syllable. Keep the vowel steady and short, like the sound in see. When you say the consonant sound, do not add friction like a buzzy hiss. Just glide smoothly like the letter y in yes.
